page.layout: One page of text. At the top, a decorative band and the title block (three centred lines of capitals and italics). Below it, one column of running text with a large woodcut initial N. At the foot, a catchword at the right.

main_text.head: AD STUDIOSOS LINGUAE HEBRAEAE, CONCLUSIO MONITORIA.
main_text.p: NON eadem semper homini mens est, non idem in humanis consilium & propositum. Nec prudentissimi quidem idem semper sentiunt, nec eodem collimant spectantque semper. Praeterit dies hodiernus, quae invenit crastinus. Probantur nunc, quae mox improbantur, si meliora succedant. Sic rerum est vicissitudo: sic mentis varietas, quia meliora quaerendo, ad perfectionem annititur. Haud dissimiliter mihi nunc evenit. Lexicon hoc ad literam [illegible, ~1 letter] exierat, neque dum vel minima de Sylloge hac vocum Rabbinicarum addenda, cogitatio animum subiverat. Superfuturae erant ad nundinas, una alterave septimana, quas inanes abire, damnosum sibi futurum, operae Typographicae conquerebantur. Sic de materia Lexici cogitans, venit in mentem studium illorum, qui apud me in lectione Rabbinica in voces quasdam subinde impegerunt, quarum usus Rabbinis erat proprius.

page.notes: The large initial N is a woodcut ornament, joined to "ON" as printed. The symbol after "literam" is not a clear Latin letter; it may be a Hebrew or Greek character, so it is marked illegible. The catchword at the foot is read as "Ut his" with a doubtful final letter. The scan is speckled, and the word "Ut" is clear; the final letters are uncertain. No running head is printed.
